comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel attempt worked against the prompt requirements for .xls reading, data parsing, safe ignoring of unsupported features, terminal/API interfaces, examples, tests, setup.py, and xlrd API exports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt received and addressed the same prompt requirements, including setup.py, xlrd/__init__.py exports, CLI/function interfaces, examples, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the task, but the parallel run also operationalized broader compatibility through an API-reference child and upstream-style tests, while the serial run covered the requirements with a smaller smoke-focused suite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent used four spawn calls, delegated API-reference and hidden-test work, and retained parent ownership of implementation and integration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had zero spawn calls and no child thread activity; one actor owned the entire lifecycle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained breadth from child investigation while accepting shared-workspace coordination risk; serial avoided coordination risk but had less independent coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The api_reference child returned a detailed compatibility surface covering modules, exports, constants, workbook behavior, sheet behavior, and date helpers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor relied on its own reading and then patched root exports, setup metadata, and CLI behavior directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a richer externalized compatibility handoff that informed the final API surface; serial had no handoff boundary and narrower self-generated compatibility evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent patched a broad upstream-style project and added setup, pyproject, API export tests, and the xlrd/__init__.py public entry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run patched a compact project, adding a JSON CLI, __main__, a small fixture, and local tests around common xlrd access paths.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel implementation path reused broader upstream behavior and tests; the serial path created a smaller targeted compatibility layer that did not satisfy every official testcase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent inspected child status, used the API-reference result, later waited on verifier children, and interrupted two still-running children only after its own verification recovered.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; the serial actor moved from implementation through local verification to finalization directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had active child lifecycle management and a recovered unfinished-verifier tail; serial had no lifecycle boundary but also no extra verifier work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The shared workspace produced a concrete collision: the hidden_tests child deleted and recreated xlrd/__init__.py while the parent owned and tested that same API entry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run modified the package boundary in a single actor and had no shared-workspace concurrent write boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main adverse parallel coordination episode: a required deliverable file was temporarily removed, causing import and CLI failures before recovery. Serial avoided that class of failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After recovering the API entry, the parent reran the full local suite to 86 passing tests, reran CLI smoke successfully, and the official evaluation passed 84 of 84.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run verified a local five-test suite, setup/API/CLI smoke checks, editable install, and CLI overview, but official evaluation passed only 83 of 84.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had substantially broader local verification aligned with upstream behavior; serial's local acceptance was too narrow to expose one hidden official failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run finished without host timeout after about 479 agent seconds, spent extra budget on child work, and interrupted remaining verifier children near closure after successful local verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also finished without host timeout after about 434 agent seconds and closed after local smoke verification, but without official-submit feedback inside the agent environment.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more coordination and token budget but converted it into broader verification and an official pass; serial used less process budget but closed with narrower evidence and one official failure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are discordant: parallel passed 84 of 84 and serial passed 83 of 84. The parallel solution benefited from a broader upstream-style implementation and verification path, including a detailed API-reference handoff, public API regression coverage, a full local pytest pass with 86 tests, editable install success, and CLI success. The serial solution created a smaller local fixture and five-test smoke suite that passed, but this narrower acceptance path did not cover one hidden official obligation. The exact failing official testcase is not mounted, so this is a supported comparative explanation rather than proof of a unique root cause.
parallel_contributors: API-reference child supplied a broad compatibility surface that the parent used for exports and behavior.
Parent reran broad upstream-style tests, editable install, and CLI smoke after repairing integration issues.
Final official evaluation passed all 84 testcases.
serial_contributors: Single actor implemented and verified a smaller custom fixture and five-test suite.
Local acceptance checks passed but official evaluation still failed one hidden testcase.
No official submit tool was available inside the agent run, so the serial agent closed without official failure detail.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial coverage was narrower than parallel coverage and likely omitted a compatibility behavior exercised by hidden tests.
Parallel incorporated an upstream-style package and sample corpus, while serial delivered a compact custom compatibility layer.
evaluator_effects: The mounted evidence contains the official pass/fail counts but not the identity of the single serial failing testcase.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
